incidents.vector: Voice phishing (vishing) calls impersonating IT support directed employees to lookalike SSO portals, where adversary-in-the-middle pages captured Microsoft 365 and Okta credentials and MFA codes in real time.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations compromised since early 2026; attackers exfiltrated SharePoint, OneDrive, Salesforce, and Zendesk data programmatically via Microsoft Graph and PowerShell, then issued extortion demands starting in the millions of dollars with escalation tactics including swatting of executives.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-20182, an authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager that grants administrative privileges remotely without credentials.
incidents.impact: CISA issued an emergency directive requiring federal agencies to patch by Sunday May 17; the controller compromise enables traffic interception, configuration tampering, and lateral access across entire SD-WAN fabrics. Cisco confirmed limited in-the-wild exploitation; the same actor has exploited Cisco edge devices for at least three years.

incidents.vector: One of six protocol vaults compromised; trading was automatically halted after the network detected abnormal signing activity.
incidents.impact: Approximately $10.7 million stolen, including 36 Bitcoin (~$3M) and $7M in other tokens. THORChain says user funds are safe and only protocol-owned funds were affected.

incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against Foxconn's North American manufacturing network; specific intrusion vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: North American factory operations disrupted; the Nitrogen group claims theft of 8 TB of data, including confidential chip drawings for Apple, Google, and NVIDIA orders. Internal messages leaked to social media.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack against corporate network; specific intrusion vector not disclosed publicly.
incidents.impact: Global business operations disrupted, including manufacturing, shipping, and receiving. Disclosed via SEC 8-K filing; some locations have restored operations.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a third-party IT services provider gave attackers access to the victim's HPE Operations Agent management platform, which was used to deploy VBScripts, register a malicious network provider DLL to harvest credentials, and plant a password filter on domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Stealthy 123-day intrusion with credential harvesting on domain controllers, web shells on internet-facing servers, and lateral movement to sensitive assets — all conducted through trusted administrative tooling without malware.

incidents.vector: Compromise of TanStack React framework npm packages spread a self-propagating credential-stealing worm across the npm registry; source code for the worm was subsequently leaked on a hacking forum with a $10,000 bounty offered for the largest follow-on attack.
incidents.impact: Nearly 400 npm packages compromised, including libraries from AI firm Mistral and automation vendor UiPath. OpenAI is rotating code-signing certificates after two employee devices were impacted. The worm wipes systems where stolen tokens are revoked.

incidents.victim: Instructure / Canvas (9,000 schools and universities, ~275M users)
incidents.vector: Repeated breaches of Instructure's Free-for-Teacher account infrastructure; ShinyHunters typically gains access via voice phishing of employees with access to Okta SSO and Salesforce.
incidents.impact: Login page defaced May 7 with extortion demand affecting schools mid-finals; data on tens of millions of students stolen (names, emails, student IDs, messages). Instructure paid the ransom and received digital confirmation of data destruction. House Homeland Security Committee summoned company leadership.

incidents.vector: Hackers had access to the utility's network for nearly two years before detection; the UK ICO faulted the company's failure to detect the intrusion.
incidents.impact: UK Information Commissioner's Office fined the utility nearly £1 million for negligence in failing to detect attackers in its network.

incidents.victim: Government entities (South America and southeastern Europe)
incidents.vector: Initial access believed to use zero-day or n-day exploits, followed by reconnaissance with Impacket and PowerShell, deployment of custom malware families (NetDraft, CloudSorcerer v3, VSHELL, SNOWLIGHT, SNOWRUST), and Active Directory credential extraction.
incidents.impact: Long-term espionage access to South American government entities since late 2024 and southeastern European government agencies during 2025. Toolset overlaps with multiple known China-nexus APT clusters.

incidents.vector: Hundreds of malicious packages were published targeting RubyGems engineers and staff, attempting cross-site scripting and credential theft on developer systems.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled new user sign-ups while investigating; the campaign targeted maintainers rather than downstream users, distinguishing it from the parallel TanStack/npm worm.

incidents.industry: Healthcare, financial services, professional services, technology
incidents.vector: Polished phishing emails masquerading as internal 'code of conduct' compliance notices led recipients through CAPTCHA gates to adversary-in-the-middle sign-in pages that proxied Microsoft authentication and stole session tokens, bypassing non-phishing-resistant MFA.
incidents.impact: Over 35,000 users targeted across 13,000 organizations between April 14-16; 92% of targets were in the United States. Successful AiTM compromises gave attackers immediate account access with stolen tokens.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social-engineering pages hosted on compromised WordPress sites lure visitors to paste and execute malicious commands that install the Vidar information stealer.
incidents.impact: ACSC issued an alert flagging targeting of Australian infrastructure with credential-stealing payloads, increasing risk of follow-on intrusion.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised vendor AVB Disc Soft's build/distribution chain and shipped a backdoored installer signed with the legitimate vendor certificate starting April 8, then selectively deployed the QUIC RAT to high-value targets.
incidents.impact: Thousands of systems received the first-stage backdoor; the second-stage QUIC RAT was deployed only to roughly a dozen targets at Russian, Belarusian, and Thai government, scientific, manufacturing, and retail entities — consistent with prior Chinese supply-chain espionage tradecraft.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to reservation systems; specific entry vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: An attacker maintained access to Best Western reservation systems for over six months (October 2025 to April 2026), affecting guests across Best Western, Sure Hotels, and WorldHotels brands.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to source-code repositories; intrusion vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Hackers obtained Trellix source code; the company says no changes were made to any of its products and notified law enforcement. Trellix is one of Europol's closest partners.

incidents.vector: Intrusion vector not publicly disclosed; attackers gained access to industrial control systems at some facilities.
incidents.impact: Five Polish water treatment facilities were hacked during 2025, with attackers reaching industrial control systems at some sites. Poland's intelligence service did not attribute the attacks publicly.

incidents.vector: Social engineering of DigiCert tech-support staff: an attacker posing as a customer convinced two support employees to run a malicious SCR (screensaver) file, exploiting a misconfigured CrowdStrike EDR agent that was disconnected from its management server.
incidents.impact: The attacker maintained access for up to two weeks, obtained 'initialization codes' from approved EV code-signing certificate orders, and successfully issued 27 EV code-signing certificates that were then used to sign Zhong Stealer malware payloads tied to cryptocurrency theft campaigns.

incidents.vector: Voter data published in a public, searchable database by a separatist political party (Republican Party of Alberta), rather than an external hack.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 2.9 million Alberta voters was publicly searchable until the province's election agency sued the party to remove it.

incidents.victim: cPanel-hosted websites (44,000+ systems, including Guam government)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a recently patched cPanel vulnerability to take over shared-hosted websites; attackers wiped public sites and posted fake $8,000 Bitcoin ransom demands on the defaced homepages.
incidents.impact: Thousands of websites defaced, including Guam government sites; the same cPanel flaw was also used to deploy cryptominers and DDoS malware. Shadowserver counted more than 44,000 compromised cPanel systems. No ransoms have been paid into the attacker wallet.
